Strong AI demand, especially for hardware and AI services.
IT services growth is steady rather than fast; the IT index fell 0.41% on 12 November.

Depends on global tech spending and how Indian companies capture AI work.

Tracks the price of gold.
Tends to hold value when stocks or the rupee fall.
Higher interest rates make gold, which pays no interest, less attractive.
Gold ETF inflows fell 22% in October.
Moves with US rate expectations; it fell about 1.2% on 12 November.
Usually held as a long-term hedge rather than for growth.
Makes speciality steel products and precision-engineered components; listed on BSE in August 2026.
IPO money is going into expanding and upgrading its factories.
Strong investor demand at listing.
First results as a listed company showed profit down 9% and operating profit down 13% from the June quarter.
Newly listed, with a short track record as a public company.
Thinly traded, so the price can swing on small volumes.
Revenue was flat-to-up (₹154 crore in the September quarter); watch whether margins recover and how the factory expansion progresses.
No guidance published yet.
Makes high-performance computing and AI servers in India, including GPU systems for government and enterprise AI projects.
AI systems are now 58% of revenue and grew more than tenfold in a year.
₹2,629 crore order book plus ₹652 crore of orders where it is the lowest bidder.
Government AI projects (IndiaAI GPU empanelment, National Supercomputing Mission 2.0 from early 2027).
Rising component prices and supply-chain issues could hurt execution.
Inventory build-up is tying up cash.
The stock is volatile: it fell more than 25% from its August high.
Management reiterated a 13–14% EBITDA margin target; revenue from the National Supercomputing Mission 2.0 is expected from early 2027.
IIFL expects sales and profit to grow about 36–37% a year from FY27 to FY29, driven by AI, private cloud and enterprise computing in India.
After results in October, Equirus, IIFL Capital and Monarch Networth all rated it Buy, with targets from ₹5,360 to ₹6,710.
India's only vertically integrated copper miner, owned by the government.
Record copper prices lifted September-quarter profit by about 182%.
₹7,000 crore plan to expand mines over 5–6 years, with a CODELCO partnership.
Restart of the Gujarat copper plant under a 20-year contract, expected around Q3 FY27.
Earnings swing with global copper prices.
Delays in mining capex or volume expansion.
The stock is well below its 52-week high of about ₹759.
The Gujarat plant restart (around Q3 FY27) and the Kendadih mine doubling to 0.4 million tonnes are the next steps.
Anand Rathi projects revenue rising about 3.3 times to roughly ₹10,200 crore between FY26 and FY31 as domestic copper demand more than doubles over the decade.
Anand Rathi rated it Buy with a ₹715 target in June 2026, before the latest results. No consensus figure was available.
Makes high-purity speciality chemicals used in medicines, nutraceuticals and food.
Buying a ready plant at Dahej SEZ to add capacity, funded from its own cash.
Indo Borax is taking a 64% controlling stake, which may bring scale.
Latest quarter: revenue up only 5%, profit down 3.6%, margins narrower.
The Indo Borax deal values promoter shares at roughly ₹103 each (₹246 crore for the stake), well below the market price.
Very small company with little analyst coverage.
Completion of the Dahej plant purchase and the Indo Borax open offer for up to 25.8% more shares.
Depends on how the new owner and extra capacity are used; neither has been spelled out.
Makes speciality fats and butters from exotic seeds (such as sal and shea) for chocolate and cosmetics makers; 61% of sales are exports.
September-quarter revenue up 41.9% and profit up 51.8%.
New capacity is coming on stream.
Growing share of higher-value products and global customers.
Seed harvests and raw-material prices can be volatile.
Heavy export reliance exposes it to currency and global demand.
Leadership roles are being reshuffled.
Management aims to turn its expanded capacity into steady growth; the price is near its 52-week high after results.
Growth depends on winning more global confectionery and cosmetics customers for its value-added fats.
All three analysts tracked rate it Strong Buy, but the average target is only about 1% above today's price.
Runs the back office for mutual funds, companies' share registries and pension funds; serves over a third of India's mutual fund industry.
Revenue up 29.9% last quarter; mutual fund client assets grew faster than the industry.
Close to 37% share of SIP accounts and fast growth in pensions.
A busy IPO market adds share-registry work.
Profit grew only 7.5% as costs rose.
A long market downturn would cut fees linked to market activity.
The acquired Ascent business earns lower margins and has Middle East exposure.
Management kept its 40% FY27 EBITDA margin target and expects issuer services to grow about 20% this year.
Growth is tied to India's rising mutual fund and pension savings and to international expansion, now about 20% of revenue.
Jefferies kept Buy but trimmed its target to ₹1,120 in October; Motilal Oswal rates it Hold at ₹1,000.
Mid-sized IT services company focused on digital transformation, AI and product engineering.
Revenue up 12.5% with full-year growth guidance of 12.5% kept.
Planned combination with ITC Infotech would create a larger company aiming for $1 billion revenue by FY28.
Analysts' average target is well above today's price.
Constant-currency growth was slower, at 6.8%.
Profit fell about 8% from the previous quarter.
Merger execution and integration risk.
Watch the progress of the ITC Infotech combination and whether 12.5% growth is delivered this year.
The combined company would have over 19,000 professionals and targets $1 billion in annual revenue by FY28.
Of six analysts, five rate it Buy or Strong Buy and one Hold.
Solar panel maker building its own solar cell and wafer capacity.
Large order book (11 GW at the last disclosure).
Module capacity rising from 4.5 GW to 17.5 GW and 12 GW of cells planned, which should lift margins.
Management guided FY27 EBITDA about 1.7 times FY26.
Profit collapsed again: September-quarter profit fell 95% to ₹5.9 crore, after an 85% fall in June.
Falling panel prices and industry oversupply.
Execution risk on the new cell plant.
After two weak quarters, the start of in-house cell production (expected by December 2026) is the key thing to watch for margins.
A 6 GW wafer-ingot project and cell capacity aim to make it more self-sufficient by FY28–FY29.
Views are split: after weak June-quarter results UBS rated it Neutral (₹215) and JM Financial Add (₹219).
Makes heat exchangers and cooling parts for air conditioners, refrigeration, data centres and buses.
H1 FY27 revenue more than doubled and profit rose 127%.
Exports nearly tripled to 22% of revenue.
New areas: data-centre and liquid cooling, bus air conditioning.
The stock has fallen sharply from its highs.
EBITDA margin narrowed in the September quarter.
Its outlook comes from the company's own press release, not independent analysis.
Management is optimistic, citing advance orders for data-centre cooling and larger capacity at Neemrana.
Growth depends on exports and new cooling segments; no numerical guidance has been given.
Only two analysts cover it; their ratings date from July 2026, before the latest results.
An exchange-traded fund that tracks an index of companies.
